why: PART THREE CLOSES ON A DATE AND A CHECK THAT FIRES IF THE DATE PASSES. Every row here carries both. A row with a date and no mechanical verification is an intention with no trigger — the failure this program has now found in the January reconstruction, the enforcement table's empty cells, the grading cron that existed and never ran, and the standing check that could not fire inside the window it protected. The `verify` field is a COMMAND, not a claim: the check runs it and reads the exit code. Nobody can mark a row done by asserting it.
not_a_todo_list: A commitment is something that becomes WRONG if the date passes unmet. Ordinary work goes in the task list. If a row here would be fine to slip, it does not belong here.

commitments.what: At least one component carries a real grade rather than no_data. Six components (survival, projection, opportunity_adj, consensus, replacement, weekly_claims) currently report no_data against their own declared bars; the rail exists and nothing calls it until weekly realized data lands.
commitments.why_that_date: Three NFL weeks after the season opens is the earliest any weekly-realized series is thick enough to grade against the declared bars. Earlier is a bar chosen to fire; later and the first month of the season is ungraded.

commitments.what: The prediction ledger reaches the graduation gate: a ledger entry can change a gate verdict, and the path is exercised end to end rather than existing as two halves.
commitments.why_that_date: Same gate as component grading — the ledger is unobservable until graded weeks exist, and pairing the dates means one re-check rather than two.

commitments.what: The January reconstruction is written into the Annual mandate with a trigger, not left as an intention. This is the ORIGINAL instance of the intention-with-no-trigger class and it is still open.
commitments.why_that_date: A January task needs its trigger installed before December ends, and December 1 leaves a month of slack rather than depending on somebody remembering in the last week.

commitments.what: Every cross-lane contract has a declared SHAPE that a consumer can test against, so a producer changing a field breaks a check rather than a renderer.
commitments.why_that_date: The in-season instrumentation deadline. After the draft the surfaces start carrying live data every week, and a shape drift found then costs a week of grading.

commitments.what: The 29x-rendered caveat stays collapsed to one instance. ALREADY DONE — this row exists so a regression fires rather than being noticed in a mock.
commitments.why_that_date: Draft day. A caveat that re-multiplies between now and then is a war-room defect on the one day it cannot be fixed.

commitments.what: The queue card's title says what the queue IS. ALREADY DONE — registered so the wording cannot drift back.
commitments.why_that_date: Draft day, same reasoning as the caveat.

commitments.what: UNKNOWN has no role: the renderer must not be able to reach a role at all when resolution is UNKNOWN. ALREADY DONE — registered because it is a contract defect that a future refactor would silently reintroduce.
commitments.why_that_date: Draft day. The explanation surface is what Cory reads to decide whether to override.

commitments.what: analyzerClaims has a weekly caller. The rail exists and nothing invokes it; a claims rail with no caller is an intention with no trigger, and any week it does not emit produces nothing for that week, permanently.
commitments.why_that_date: Cory's stated in-season instrumentation deadline, and the first NFL Sunday is the first week that can be lost. This is the BUILD half of item 32 — the championship-probability claim surface is REJECTED (28 of 36 against a naive 27 of 36, CI spanning zero).

commitments.what: Every roster-construction result produced this week is re-run against the REAL pick schedule once the slate confirms. Two schedules were used and they disagree: '12 picks from 34' (assumes only Cory's three keepers exist) and the slot-8 snake 33/48/53 (assumes none). They produce different rosters -- TE 1 under one, TE 2 under the other. NEITHER IS REAL. A one-pick offset changed the constructed roster more than a 30-point shift in RB replacement did, so nothing built on an assumed schedule can be graded until the true one is known.
commitments.why_that_date: Keeper lock. The slate confirms which keepers cost which picks, which is the only thing that resolves the schedule, and it lands two days before the draft -- so this is the last date on which a wrong schedule is still correctable.

commitments.what: Grade the pre-season unprojected snapshot. draft/data/unprojected_snapshot.json lists the 1181 players the board could not rank in August (proj_mean 0, vorp a position constant). The engine REFUSES them. That refusal is currently ungraded: nobody knows whether ignoring them cost real players. Join on player_id against realized season points and count how many finished top-24 at their position.
commitments.why_that_date: After the fantasy season ends, when realized points exist for a full year. Earlier and the sample is partial; later and the next board build has replaced the projections this was true of.

commitments.what: A report-only diagnostic over the board artifact: (a) VALUE SPIKE — numeric fields where an implausible share of players carry one exact value (1181 sat at proj_mean 0, absence written as a number); (b) RATIO LOCK — field pairs whose ratio is constant across the population (proj_sd = 0.25*proj_mean and proj_ceiling = 1.35*proj_mean, the defect that made the ceiling term collinear with value and left two of eight weights UNMEASURED). It must REPORT AND NEVER DECIDE: replacement level, caps, floors and ONESIE_KEEP all produce legitimate identical values, so a cliff is a DETECTOR, NOT A DEFINITION.
commitments.why_that_date: After the draft and before the in-season cadence hardens. Cory ruled it explicitly out of the pre-draft window on 2026-08-13: a data-quality diagnostic moves no recommendation, and the nine days before the draft belong to what the board does wrong.
